title: Process Launched From Synthetic User-Writable Temporary Path
detection_hypothesis: If an adversary stages tooling in a user-writable directory, the resulting process creation event will show an Image path rooted in a temporary or public directory rather than in a managed installation directory.

field_semantics.Image: Absolute path of the executable backing the created process.

collection_prerequisites: A process creation source is enabled (Sysmon Event ID 1 or Security Event ID 4688).
Command-line auditing is enabled when Security 4688 is the only available source.
expected_collection_gaps: Security 4688 without command-line auditing provides no CommandLine value.
Short-lived processes may be lost if the agent is restarted during collection.
normalization_assumptions: Image and ParentImage are absolute paths using backslash separators.
CommandLine retains the original argument order and spacing.
ingestion_differences: Some pipelines lowercase paths; the lab matcher is case-insensitive by default.
Sysmon and 4688 differ in parent process fidelity and in User field formatting.
retention_considerations: Process creation is high volume; 30 to 90 days of hot retention is typical.
expected_volume: Low to moderate on managed endpoints; higher on developer workstations.
false_positive_strategy: Benign matches concentrate around packaged installers, patch management, and developer workstations. Tune with the writing or launching process identity and with the specific binary name rather than excluding the temporary directory tree.
tuning_guidance: Prefer per-binary exclusions anchored on Image endswith plus a signature or hash condition. Do not exclude the whole AppData\Local\Temp prefix, because that removes the detection value of the rule entirely.
test_strategy: Positive cases execute from the per-user and machine temporary directories. Negative cases cover managed installation directories, the system directory, and the explicitly allowed patch installer.
unmapped_defensive_objects_reason: No Detection Strategy, Analytic, or Data Component identifier for this technique was present in the pinned ATT&CK extraction used by this lab. Defensive arrays are left empty rather than populated with unverified identifiers. Unmapped techniques: T1204.002.
author: Salvatore Mazzaglia
